macro_context.market_sentiment: Strongly bullish on May 6 — Nasdaq +2.02% to 25,838, S&P 500 +1.46% to record 7,365, Dow +1.24% to 49,910 — driven by reports the US and Iran are nearing a peace agreement and semiconductor earnings beats from AMD and Supermicro. DIS was among the top Dow movers at +6.24%.
macro_context.fed_outlook: Fed held rates steady at 3.5%-3.75% on April 29 (third consecutive hold) with an 8-4 vote split — most dissents since 1992. Median FOMC projection forecasts just one rate cut in 2026; inflation remains elevated above 2% target partly due to energy prices and tariffs. Powell stepping down as Chair but remaining on the board.
macro_context.geopolitical: US-Iran war is the dominant flashpoint; potential peace deal catalyzed today's market rally and oil price decline. Additional tensions: US intervention in Venezuela, NATO posture in Greenland, ongoing tariff uncertainty, and US midterm elections. Chinese overcapacity in tech/industrial sectors is a secondary European risk.
key_events: US-Iran peace deal negotiations — outcome would significantly affect oil prices and risk sentiment
Fed next meeting (June 2026) — markets pricing no change but any signal shift would move equities
US midterm elections 2026 — policy uncertainty for entertainment, media, and consumer sectors
Paramount-Skydance/Warner Bros. Discovery merger completion — reshapes streaming competitive landscape

ticker_news.headline: Disney Q2 FY2026 earnings beat: revenue $25.17B vs $24.84B estimate; EPS $1.57 vs $1.49 estimate; DIS +6.24% on the day
CEO Josh D'Amaro speaks to investors for first time after Q2 results; FY2026 adjusted EPS growth guidance raised to ~12%, FY2027 double-digit growth guided
The Mandalorian and Grogu feature film arriving theaters May 22 — first major Disney theatrical release of the summer season
Big Thunder Mountain Railroad reopened May 3 at Magic Kingdom after 1+ year refurbishment; new backstory and lower height requirement expected to boost park attendance
Motley Fool: 'Is This the Week Disney Stock Finally Wakes Up?' — noting DIS was down ~10% YTD entering earnings week and historically cheap vs. historical valuation

analyst_consensus.recent_changes: Raymond James upgraded DIS to Outperform from Market Perform in April 2026 with $115 PT, citing historical cheapness after ~15% YTD decline. Guggenheim maintained Buy with $140 PT (February 2026). Earlier Q1 2026 headwinds prompted some downgrades. Current distribution: 17 Buy, 5 Hold, 1 Sell across ~23 analysts (Benzinga $129.08 avg across 25 analysts; MarketBeat $133.53; median of 42 analysts $131.00, range $77-$160). Stock was ~$104 pre-earnings, implying ~25-30% upside to consensus targets.

web_context.competitor_activity: Netflix leads streaming with 325M subscribers and $20B content spend in 2026 — widening its lead over Disney+. Paramount-Skydance agreed to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery, combining Paramount+/HBO Max/Pluto into a rival with a projected 22% US streaming share, creating a more formidable consolidated competitor. Universal's Epic Universe theme park saw 12% attendance growth in March vs Disney World's steadier 3%, signaling growing theme park competition. Comcast is spinning off its cable TV networks into Versant Media Group, restructuring the legacy media landscape. Disney itself is spending $24B on content in FY2026 to defend its streaming and franchise positions.
web_context.earnings_info: Q2 FY2026 reported today May 6, 2026: EPS $1.57 (beat est. $1.49), Revenue $25.17B (beat est. $24.84B), operating income beat prior company guidance. FY2026 adjusted EPS growth guidance raised to approximately 12%; company also guided for double-digit EPS growth in FY2027. Next earnings (Q3 FY2026) expected around August 2026.
